author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The U.S. Treasury Department announced new sanctions Thursday against companies and individuals it says support Hezbollah and other Iranian-aligned groups, expanding Washington’s economic campaign during the continuing regional conflict.

The Office of Foreign Assets Control targeted people and entities in Iraq, the United Arab Emirates, Lebanon and Turkey. Treasury said the networks supported Kata’ib Hezbollah, an Iraqi paramilitary group linked to Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps, and Lebanon’s Hezbollah.

The measures fall under Operation Economic Outcast, a campaign Treasury announced August 24 to restrict funding tied to Iran’s military, missile development, cyber activity and the Revolutionary Guard. OFAC also said it would deny most Iran-related license requests except in exceptional circumstances. Separately, a U.S. citizen agreed to pay $1.43 million to resolve potential civil liability involving 39 apparent sanctions violations.

The newest designations did not target Yemen’s Houthis, whose Red Sea advances are creating a separate threat to shipping. The practical effect of the latest sanctions will depend on enforcement and the ability of designated networks to find alternative financial channels.
dek: Treasury targeted entities and individuals in four countries and tightened its approach to Iran-related licensing as the regional conflict continues.
headline: U.S. expands sanctions on networks tied to Iranian proxies
